title.narrative: National Gini index

description.narrative: The Gini index provides a summary measure of the degree of inequality and may be calculated using either income or consumption data. It measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. The Gini index is the Gini coefficient expressed as a percentage ranging from 0 which represents perfect equality to 100 which implies perfect inequality. For methodology see: https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SI.POV.GINI.

title.narrative: Country score according to the CIVICUS Monitor

description.narrative: Each country is assigned a rating as follows: open, narrowed, obstructed, repressed or closed. CIVICUS Monitor recognises that ratings alone may offer a crude measure of the state of civic space in any given context, which is why it emphasises the importance of uptodate, locallygenerated analysis to complement the ratings. Nonetheless, a rating system enables useful comparisons to be made across different countries, and also encourages the tracking of a countrys overall civic space conditions over time.
